toml:
# Celeste IOD signal designs: the frequency bands and the "Classical Pilot" signal
# configuration #1 of ESA's Celeste In-Orbit Demonstration (IOD) low Earth orbit (LEO)
# positioning, navigation and timing (PNT) mission, as parameterised signal designs.
#
# THIS FILE IS THE ONLY PLACE IN THE REPOSITORY THAT HOLDS WORKSHOP-DERIVED NUMBERS.
# Every carrier, bandwidth, allocation, component structure and shape target below
# marked WORKSHOP was presented at the ESA NAVISP LEO-PNT workshop, 2026 (the
# Navigation Innovation and Support Programme), and cleared for use; no Celeste signal
# specification is public. Nothing else in the engine depends on this file, and nothing
# compiles it in (it is a repository-only scenario, not bundled into the binary):
# deleting it removes Celeste from a release, and every other scenario, test and oracle
# still runs. See docs/LEO-SIGNAL.md.
#
# What the IOD is for, in ESA's own public words: an in-orbit demonstration of 11
# satellites plus a spare that tests radionavigation signals in several bands
# (https://www.esa.int/Applications/Satellite_navigation/Celeste/Celeste_IOD_-_Facts_and_figures).
# The IOD signals are a vehicle for experiments; later phases (Celeste In-Orbit
# Pathfinder, a European Union LEO-PNT layer) will use their own signal designs, which
# is why these are presets of a general signal model, not "the Celeste signal".
#
# Bands presented (WORKSHOP), with the ITU service allocation:
#   E5    1191.795 MHz  RNSS      51.15 MHz  (the Galileo E5 centre; 5 x 10.23 MHz wide)
#   SR    2492.028 MHz  RDSS      15 MHz
#   SM    2170.00 MHz   MSS       0.2 MHz and 5 MHz (for 5G non-terrestrial-network terminals)
#   UHF   465.465 MHz   EESS      10 MHz
#   C     5019.861 MHz  RNSS      19.7 MHz
#   Cext  5071.011 MHz (B1) and 5122.161 MHz (B2), non-RNSS, 120 MHz and 240 MHz
# (RNSS Radio Navigation Satellite Service, RDSS Radio Determination Satellite Service,
# MSS Mobile Satellite Service, EESS Earth Exploration-Satellite Service.)
#
# Configuration #1, "Classical Pilot" (WORKSHOP), BPSK(n) = binary phase-shift keying at
# n x 1.023 Mchip/s, FDMA = frequency-division multiple access:
#   E5#1   pilot BPSK(10); data PfA BPSK(1) or PfB BPSK(10); no acquisition component
#   S#1    pilot BPSK(5);  data BPSK(1) FDMA; acquisition BPSK(1/3) FDMA
#   UHF#1  as S#1
#   CR#1   pilot BPSK(10); data BPSK(10); acquisition BPSK(1/3)
#
# ASSUMPTIONS (not presented, each labelled on its component): the power splits (pilot
# 50 %, the rest shared equally); the code lengths (one 1 ms period; BPSK(1/3) over 1 ms
# is 341 chips); the FDMA sub-carrier offsets (S#1 at -6.0 and -3.3 MHz, where the
# measured IOD S-band spectrum shown at the workshop has narrow components, which
# component sits on which being an assumption; UHF#1 at -4.0 and -2.2 MHz, scaled to the
# 10 MHz band); and, for the SM and Cext bands, whose modulation was not presented, a
# REPRESENTATIVE single BPSK component sized to the band. The orbit altitude, 510 km,
# is public (GMV, https://www.ion.org/gnss/abstracts.cfm?paperID=16907; Thales Alenia
# Space press release).
#
# The [[shape_checks]] entry holds the E5#1 PfA design's band-limited spectrum against
# the measured IOD E5 spectrum shown at the workshop: a narrow central BPSK(1)-like peak
# on a BPSK(10)-like main lobe with nulls near +/-10 MHz, and sidelobes near +/-15 MHz
# some 22 to 25 dB below the peak (IOD-1 peaked near -133 dBW/Hz, sidelobes about -155 to
# -158 dBW/Hz). MODELLED consistency only: the measurement has no published calibration,
# so shapes are compared, not levels.
#
# The C/N0 sweep reaches 57.5 dB-Hz, the peak of the IOD pass shown at the workshop
# (a bell-shaped pass from about 41 to 57.5 dB-Hz over some 200 s, 7 to 10 dB above the
# Galileo satellites tracked beside it).
kind = "leo-signal"

[receiver]
noise_figure_db = 2.0
antenna_temp_k = 290.0
cn0_dbhz = [40.0, 45.0, 50.0, 55.0, 57.5]
reference_cn0_dbhz = 50.0
loop_bandwidth_hz = 1.0
integration_time_s = 0.02
correlator_spacings_chips = [1.0, 0.5, 0.2, 0.1]
reference_spacing_chips = 0.5
tracking_threshold_dbhz = 25.0

[acquisition]
altitude_km = 510.0
oscillator_ppm = 0.5
coherent_ms = 1.0
noncoherent = 1
pfa_cell = 1e-4

[trade]
reference_signal = "celeste-iod-e5-1-pfa"
slant_tec_tecu = 50.0
slant_range_km = 1000.0

[[signals]]
name = "celeste-iod-e5-1-pfa"
system = "Celeste IOD"
source = "WORKSHOP"
source_ref = "presented at the ESA NAVISP LEO-PNT workshop, 2026"
centre_mhz = 1191.795
tx_bandwidth_mhz = 51.15
allocation = "rnss"
orbit_altitude_km = 510.0
notes = "E5#1 Classical Pilot, data option PfA."

[[signals.components]]
role = "pilot"
modulation = "BPSK(10)"
power_fraction = 0.5
code_length_chips = 10230
note = "power split and code length assumed"

[[signals.components]]
role = "data"
modulation = "BPSK(1)"
power_fraction = 0.5
code_length_chips = 1023
note = "PfA; power split and code length assumed"
